summary: B5 audio and haptics: DONE, verified in EditMode, PlayMode and a built Windows player run with sound on. SfxSynth (new) synthesizes the 13 contract 16 clips at startup with pure C# DSP (doubles, deterministic xorshift noise, sine voices with exponential pitch glides, TPT state-variable filters, raised-cosine attacks, exponential decays, 12 dB/oct low-pass, optional tanh squeeze, no square or saw waves), then AudioClip.Create (mono, 44.1 kHz, non-streamed). Clips: ExitPlop 0.16 s (droplet bubble gliding 520 to 1350 Hz), ReturnGloop 0.34 s (two low bubbles and a body), FillSwell 0.55 s (band-passed noise whoosh sweeping up under a soft C major chord, sized to FillDuration 0.35 s), CutSnap 0.18 s (bright falling pluck 3400 to 1500 Hz over a 3 ms high click and a short noise tsk), SparkLoop 0.5 s seamless loop (fizzing band of noise with crackles, two heartbeat thumps with glassy ticks per loop, 330/334 Hz drone beating at the 4 Hz pulse rate; every component periodic, filters primed over a full pass), CaughtSplat 0.5 s (wet low-pass burst closing down, sinking blob, 7 droplets), RingChime 0.9 s (C6 then G6 bell), LassoZip 0.42 s (accelerating clicks over a rising swoop, ended by a bubble), ToastTick 0.09 s, UiClick 0.07 s (bubble pop), CountdownTick 0.13 s (marimba-like E6), WinJingle 1.5 s (rising liquid C major arpeggio), LoseJingle 1.4 s (falling G4 Eb4 C4, last note sagging). Every clip is normalized to peak 0.89; one-shots start and end on exact zeros. Measured: 6.7 s of audio synthesized in 129 ms in the Windows Mono player. Sfx (replaces the stub) is built by Sfx.Create(GameDirector): 12 pooled 2D AudioSources plus one loop source. It binds on SessionStarted (also re-raised on attract restarts) and subscribes to the session's EventRaised. It follows StateChanged (Results plays the win jingle for rank 1, the lose jingle otherwise, once per session) and PausedChanged. Scope rules of contract 16: while the human plays a real round (alive, State Playing), events where the human is Player or Other play at 0 dB. Bot-only Exit/Return/Cut/Eliminated play only when their point is in the main camera view (Camera.main, 3 % margin), at -12 dB, at most one per type every 0.25 s; cut snaps are exempt (0.05 s duplicate guard) and the human's cuts are louder (0 dB). In Menu (attract) and after the human's elimination, only UI sounds play, plus on-screen events at -18 dB. The spark tension loop plays only for the human's own chase: pitch = 1 + 0.9 k^1.6 with k = 1 - eta/4 s clamped (1.0 far, 1.9 imminent), so the pulse rate goes from 4/s to 7.6/s. Volume goes from 0.55 to 1 with eta. It fades in over 0.06 s and out over 0.15 s, stops at once on the catch, pause or a new session, drops 0 to 20 % in slow motion, and stays silent while the ready gate waits. The countdown ticks once per HUD second over the last 10 s, pitched up a major third for the last 3. 23.3 debounce: the exit plop waits for GameSession.HasVisibleDetach (trail > 0.35 u or exit >= 0.25 s). The return gloop plays only for a Return with cells, after a visible detach, or for a chased return. The fill swell plays for every human Return with cells, its gain scaled -6..0 dB with the captured cell count. Muting: SaveData.SoundOn false stops every voice at once. Batchmode and -mute hard-mute: no clip is synthesized and nothing plays, but every decision still runs and raises CuePlayed, so the PlayMode and EditMode tests exercise the logic. Sfx also guarantees exactly one AudioListener: it adds a fallback on its own GameObject only when the camera has none, and removes it when another appears. Haptics (replaces the stub): Pulse(int ms) never throws. The real code runs only on Android players (UNITY_ANDROID && !UNITY_EDITOR) and returns at once when SaveData.HapticsOn is false. It uses the Android Vibrator through AndroidJavaObject: VibrationEffect.createOneShot(ms, DEFAULT_AMPLITUDE) when SDK_INT >= 26, vibrate(long) before. Every JNI call has its own try/catch, and the first failure logs one warning and disables haptics. The unreachable 'if (s_NeverTrue) Handheld.Vibrate();' sits inside AndroidPulse, which Pulse calls, for the VIBRATE permission. The JNI code is also compiled in the editor, so a type error shows in every compile. Durations come from the contract (Sfx calls them on the human's live events): cut received 60, cut dealt 30, caught 120, saved return while chased 40, capture 20 ms. VERIFICATION: dotnet compile of the 3 files plus the tests against the Unity 6000.3.23f1 engine DLLs under the editor, Android-player and Windows-player define sets (0 warnings, 0 errors). EditMode SfxTests: 11/11 green (TestResults/B5_edit.xml), also green inside the full run. Full EditMode: 357 tests, 353 passed, 2 skipped (explicit Core cases), 2 failed in B2's ActorViewsTests (not B5). PlayMode: 7 tests, the 3 BootTests that boot the whole game (Sfx included) green, 1 failure in B3's SteeringInputPlayTests (not B5). BuildWindows -buildOut Build/B5 succeeded. DevShot run of Build/B5 with sound allowed and -sfxlog: exit 0, scenario PASS, 7 PNGs, zero exceptions or errors in player.log. The cue sequence was exactly as designed: attract plop -18 dB in the menu, human plop 0 dB, on-screen bot plop -12 dB, cut snap and tension loop (pitch 1.03 at the first cut, 1.51 at the second), gloop and full swell on the saved chased return, second plop, lasso zip, cut, splat, lose jingle (rank 4e on results.png), spectator gloop at -18 dB after the death. AudioListener output peaks of 0.20 to 0.56 prove the audio reached the mixer without clipping. I looked at CutDroplets.png and results.png: the game renders, HUD and results are consistent with the cues. I also looked at spectrograms of all 13 clips (TestResults/B5_sfx/spectrograms.png): rising bubble hooks, falling cut pluck, loop thumps under the fizz band, accelerating zip clicks, rising and falling jingle notes.

static class SfxSynth: consts SampleRate 44100, ClipCount 13, PeakTarget 0.89f, PeakLimit 0.95f, SparkLoopSeconds 0.5, SparkLoopPulses 2, TensionFarEta 4.0, TensionBasePitch 1f, TensionTopPitch 1.9f, TensionBaseVolume 0.55f, TensionTopVolume 1f; double DurationOf(SfxId); int SampleCount(SfxId); bool IsLoop(SfxId); float[] Generate(SfxId) (pure, deterministic); AudioClip CreateClip(SfxId) (mono, named 'pio_<id>'); float TensionCloseness(double eta), TensionPitch(double eta), TensionRate(double eta) (pulses per second), TensionVolume(double eta), all non-increasing in eta, +inf and NaN treated as far.

Sfx (MonoBehaviour, contract factory Sfx.Create(GameDirector) kept): static Sfx Instance; static void PlayUiClick() and static void PlayToastTick() (for B4: null-safe, rate limited 0.03 s / 0.1 s, play in every state unless sound is off); static float BaseVolume(SfxId); event Action<SfxCue> CuePlayed (every sound decision, also when muted); event Action<int> HapticPulsed (every haptic request in ms, also off Android); bool HardMuted (batchmode or -mute), bool Muted (HardMuted or !SaveData.SoundOn), bool ClipsReady, bool TensionActive, float TensionPitch, float TensionLevel; consts VoiceCount 12, OnScreenMargin 0.03f, TensionFadeInSeconds 0.06f, TensionFadeOutSeconds 0.15f, CutRepeatSeconds 0.05f, UiRepeatSeconds 0.03f, ToastRepeatSeconds 0.1f, CountdownSeconds 10, CountdownUrgentSeconds 3, CountdownUrgentPitch 1.26f, SwellFullCells 1500; test hooks void Attach(GameSession, GameState), void SetAttachedState(GameState), void Tick(float unscaledDeltaTime) (Update calls it), void Teardown() (OnDestroy calls it; edit-mode tests call it before DestroyImmediate).
struct SfxCue { SfxId Id; float GainDb; float Pitch; int Player; bool Audible; } (Sfx.cs).

static class SfxScope (Sfx.cs): consts HumanGainDb 0, BotGainDb -12, SpectatorGainDb -18, RateLimitSeconds 0.25f; float? EventGainDb(bool live, bool involvesHuman, bool onScreen); bool IsScopedType(SimEventType) (Exit, Return, Cut, Eliminated); float DbToGain(float db).

Haptics: consts CutReceivedMs 60, CutDealtMs 30, CaughtMs 120, SavedReturnMs 40, CaptureMs 20, MaxPulseMs 1000 (longer requests clamped); bool Disabled (true after the first JNI failure). Pulse(int ms) signature unchanged.

Command-line flag -sfxlog (any player): logs every cue ('[Sfx] cue gain= pitch=

player=') and the AudioListener output peak once per second ('[Sfx] output peak=...'). Startup log line '[PainterIO] Sfx: 13/13 clips synthesized (...) in ms' when not hard-muted.
contract_issues: 23.3 has two sentences about short exits. Sentence 1: ignore an exit whose Return has empty Cells and that lasted < 0.25 s. Sentence 2: the plop starts when the trail exceeds 0.35 u or the exit has lasted 0.25 s, and the return sound plays for a Return with cells or after a visible detach. They disagree for an exit of 0.06 to 0.25 s whose trail passed 0.35 u and whose Return captured nothing. Sound cannot know the future at exit time, so B5 applies sentence 2: the plop played, so the gloop plays too. The diagonal-edge flicker that motivated sentence 1 (1 to 2 tick exits, trail < 0.2 u) stays silent either way.

16 'ring chime' does not say spawn or pickup. B5 plays it at 0 dB when the human picks the ring, and a softer, lower chime (-12 dB, pitch 0.84) on RingSpawned during a live round. RingSpawned is a world event, not a bot-only one, so it is not limited to on-screen points. Bot LassoPocket / RingPicked and all LassoCrossNoCharge events are silent: they are not in the contract's bot list.
16 'at most one per type every 0.25 s; the cut snap plays on every on-screen cut' is read as: cut snaps are exempt from the 0.25 s limit. A 0.05 s guard only drops exact duplicates in the same frame.
16 lists no haptic for an elimination by TerritoryLost: none is played (the splat sound plays). A chased Return that also captured gives one 40 ms pulse (saved), not 40 + 20.
16 lists 'toast tick' but toasts belong to B4 (15.3). Sfx cannot see when a toast is shown, so it exposes Sfx.PlayToastTick() for B4 to call (see needs).
open_issues: The sounds were never heard by a human ear (an agent cannot listen). They are verified by numbers: lengths, peaks, exact-zero ends, the seamless loop, monotonic tension, and the listener output peaks in the player log. Spectrograms were checked too. Please audition TestResults/B5_sfx/*.wav (SparkLoop.wav repeats the loop 8 times). Balance is set in Sfx.BaseVolumes (one float per clip) and the timbres in SfxSynth: both are easy to retune after a listen.

Haptics not tried on a device: no Android build by B5 and no device attached. The JNI path compiles in the editor (UNITY_EDITOR) and was compiled with UNITY_ANDROID player defines in a dotnet check; B6's Android build compiles it for real and Builder checks VIBRATE.

Startup synthesis costs 129 ms once in GameDirector.Awake on the Windows Mono player (dev PC). Android IL2CPP is unmeasured (expect roughly 100 to 300 ms one-time). Clip memory is about 1.2 MB (6.7 s of float PCM).
Bot sounds and spectator sounds need the main camera (Camera.main) for the on-screen test. Without a camera they stay silent; human sounds do not depend on it.

Not B5: in the full runs, B2's ActorViewsTests.B2_RetractionFrontNeverOverlapsThePearl (1e-8 tolerance) and B2_TrailCurvePassesThroughSimPoints, and B3's SteeringInputPlayTests.Touch_FloatingStickOwnsTheFirstFingerOnly, were failing at the time of my run (owners mid-iteration).

FYI for B4 (not B5): in TestResults/B5_devshot/CutDroplets.png the danger vignette covers about half the screen in saturated red. It may be heavier than the contract's 'pulsing white/red edge' (could be the pulse peak).
needs: B4 (UI): call Sfx.PlayUiClick() from every Button and Toggle onClick (UiKit), and Sfx.PlayToastTick() when a toast becomes visible. Both are static, null-safe and rate limited, and play in every state (menu, pause, results) unless sound is off. SaveData.SoundOn toggles take effect at once, nothing else needed.

B3 (camera): keep an AudioListener on the main camera and the 'MainCamera' tag. Sfx adds a fallback listener only when none exists and removes it when one appears. The bot/spectator on-screen test uses Camera.main.

B6 (probe/verify): the probe's -mute hard-mutes Sfx (no clip synthesized) while every decision still runs. Optional: subscribe to Sfx.Instance.CuePlayed / HapticPulsed to assert the DemoScenario cue order, as SfxTests.Sfx_DemoRoundPlaysTheHumanCuesAndHapticsInOrder does headless. -sfxlog adds a cue trace to any player run. The Android build compiles the Haptics JNI path and the Handheld.Vibrate reference.

Contract owner: fold the readings listed under contract_issues into section 16 (ring chime on pickup plus a soft spawn chime, cut snaps exempt from the 0.25 s limit, Sfx.PlayToastTick called by B4, no haptic on TerritoryLost, sentence 2 of 23.3 for sounds).
